faq.q: What is a good song for a wedding slideshow?
faq.a: A good slideshow song fits the photos on screen and has a lyric you’ve heard all the way through. Reliable picks: “In My Life” by The Beatles for childhood photos, “Lucky” by Jason Mraz and Colbie Caillat for dating, “Lean on Me” by Bill Withers for friends, and “What a Wonderful World” by Louis Armstrong to close. Choose songs that mean something to the two of you over whatever is trending.

faq.q: How many songs should a wedding slideshow have?
faq.a: One song for every 3 to 4 minutes of slideshow. A 5-minute sit-down slideshow usually needs one or two songs, a 7-minute one needs two, and a 10-minute rehearsal dinner slideshow needs about three. Change songs at a chapter break so the new music signals the next part of the story, and fade between them rather than cutting.

faq.q: Can I use copyrighted songs in a wedding slideshow?
faq.a: For the room, ask your DJ or venue coordinator how they handle music. Online is where problems start: platforms match uploads against registered songs, and a slideshow with a commercial track can be blocked, muted or have ads placed on it. Keep the full-music version for the reception and post a version with royalty-free music or a song added through the platform’s own music picker.

faq.q: What song should end a wedding slideshow?
faq.a: Pick something big and warm with a clear ending, so the last photo can hold while the music fades. “What a Wonderful World” by Louis Armstrong, “Home” by Phillip Phillips and “Thinking Out Loud” by Ed Sheeran are dependable closers. End on photos of the guests in the room, then hold the final image for 8 to 10 seconds before the screen goes dark.

faq.q: Should a wedding slideshow use instrumental music?
faq.a: Use instrumental music when words would compete with something else: captions, voice notes, a speech that leads into the slideshow, or a loop playing quietly under dinner conversation. For a short sit-down showing, a song with lyrics usually lands harder. You can also mix both, with an instrumental under the childhood captions and a lyric song for the finale.

faq.q: Where can I find royalty-free music for a wedding video?
faq.a: Start with the YouTube Audio Library, which is free in YouTube Studio and marks which tracks need an artist credit. Paid stock-music services sell licenses for online video if you want more choice. For a short reel of the wedding itself, Filmsera’s recap includes 6 built-in royalty-free songs licensed under Creative Commons Attribution, so credit the artist when you post.
